newsitem.title: UK: Unilever boss wants phased EMU introduction.
newsitem.headline: Unilever boss wants phased EMU introduction.

text.p: Niall FitzGerald, chairman of Anglo-Dutch food and consumer products group Unilever, said on Thursday he favoured a phased introduction of a single European currency.
In a speech at the London School of Economics, FitzGerald said a phased start of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would be the best guarantee of its success.
FitzGerald, who is widely known for his pro-European stance, said a group of unnamed countries was on track to proceed with EMU in 1999.
"The economies of the so-called "first wave core" have converged sufficiently to ensure the project's success," FitzGerald said.
"It is essential, however, that politics does not come before economics in deciding the size of the initial core group," he added.
EMU might be dealt a "mortal blow" if countries which do not meet the economic criteria were allowed to participate, FitzGerald said.
He again urged Britain to help shape EMU and not stay sidelined in any discussions on a single currency.
"Such a policy could be disastrous," he said.
